title: Eye-gaze as sole input: the Midas touch problem
bottleneck: Using gaze alone for selection means everything you look at risks activation: the Midas touch problem. Dwell-time selection is slow and tiring, blink detection misfires, and distinguishing inspection from intention needs extra modalities. Gaze is a fast pointer but a terrible clicker.
why_it_blocks: Hands-free AR/VR interaction needs gaze to work alone for accessibility and convenience, but false activations make it untrustworthy. Gaze input stays a complement, never the primary channel.
current_state: Gaze-plus-pinch and gaze-plus-voice hybrids are standard, sidestepping the problem rather than solving it. Pure-gaze interfaces remain slow and error-prone. Dwell-based selection forces users to stare unnaturally, causing fatigue and accidental activations that erode trust. Combining gaze with micro-gestures helps, but every added modality raises cost, calibration burden, and failure modes.
